name: Kambara
sum: Eocene mekosuchine from Queensland, a semi-aquatic generalist and one of the oldest Australian crocodylians.
wsnote: Mature specimens generally 3–4 m; a large mandible of K. implexidens suggests up to 3.5 m for that species.
holotype: Type material of K. murgonensis from Murgon, Queensland (Willis et al. 1993).
material: Skulls, jaws and limb bones of four species from Murgon and the Rundle Formation.
biology: Lived like many modern crocodiles; its limb bones suggest it walked on land better than Australia's living crocodiles.
author: Willis et al. 1993
